mainTopic: The shape of the לחם הפנים, its status during the desert journeys, and the holiness of the camps when the משכן was taken apart
overview: The amud first finishes the argument about the shape of the לחם הפנים. A ברייתא about a square tablet seems to challenge the view that the bread looked like a rocking boat. The גמרא answers that only the mold's opening was square, and a second ברייתא about forked golden supports backs the rocking-boat view. Next comes a new question: when the משכן was taken apart and carried in the desert, did the לחם הפנים become פסול? רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי disagree, and each side brings a פסוק and answers the other's פסוק. רב דימי reframes the dispute as being only about bread removed from the שולחן. A ברייתא and a מה נפשך argument then knock out that version. רבין concludes that there is no dispute: bread still arranged on the שולחן stays kosher, and removed bread becomes פסול. אביי learns from the ברייתא that the משכן could be taken apart even at night. Then רב אשי settles a contradiction between two ברייתות about זבין and מצורעין by saying they follow רבי אליעזר and the רבנן, whose ברייתא begins at the end of the amud.

steps.title: A ברייתא describes the bread as looking like a square tablet
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא saying the bread's mold looked like a square tablet. This seems to clash with the view that the bread was shaped like a rocking boat.
steps.simpleTranslation: They objected: The bread had a mold in the oven shaped like a reed basket, and it looked like a four-cornered tablet!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the opinion that the לחם הפנים looked like a rocking boat. It uses a ברייתא that describes something square.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A rocking boat is narrow at the bottom and open at the top. A "four-cornered tablet" sounds flat and square. So the ברייתא seems to say the bread was square, which goes against the rocking-boat view.

keyTerms.meaning: A beehive or reed basket. Here it is the mold the bread was baked in.
A four-cornered (square or rectangular) tablet
Oven

phrases.english: They raised an objection: something like a reed basket
phrases.notes: This is a mold that held the dough while it baked.

phrases.english: it had in the oven,
and it looked like a kind of four-cornered tablet!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the argument from the earlier part of the daf about the shape of the bread
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that the לחם הפנים looked like a rocking boat
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא calls the shape a square tablet, which does not fit a boat shape.

steps.title: Only the opening of the mold was square
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the ברייתא. Only the top opening was square, so the bottom could still narrow down like a boat.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: its opening looked like a four-cornered tablet.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the rocking-boat view. It explains that the ברייתא was describing only the top of the mold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once "square" refers only to the opening, there is no contradiction. A boat-shaped bread can have a four-cornered top and still narrow toward the bottom.

keyTerms.meaning: "Say". The גמרא uses it to reread a source differently.
Its opening, meaning the top part

phrases.english: Say: and its opening looked
like a kind of four-cornered tablet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 1
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the ברייתא so it describes only part of the shape
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the whole bread was square.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the top opening was square. The bread itself could still be boat-shaped.

steps.title: Golden forked supports show the bread was boat-shaped
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא describes four golden supports with forked tops that held the bread. It says outright that the bread looked like a rocking boat.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא supports the one who said it looked like a rocking boat: There were four golden supports there. They split at their tops like forked branches, and the bread rested on them, because it looked like a rocking boat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports the rocking-boat opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא explains why the supports had to be forked. The bread was boat-shaped, so it needed support on its sloping sides. It also says plainly that the bread looked like a rocking boat.

keyTerms.meaning: A rocking boat
Support panels or poles
Forked branches, like pitchforks

steps.whatToRemember: The rocking-boat view survives the challenge and gets support from a ברייתא.

phrases.english: It is taught in line with the one who said
like a rocking boat,
as it is taught: four supports of gold
were there,
phrases.notes: "There" means on the שולחן, the Table that held the bread.

phrases.english: split at their tops
they were like forked branches,
for they would rest the bread on them,
since it looked like a kind of rocking boat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending the rocking-boat view, the גמרא now brings positive support for it
steps.raayaObject: The view that the לחם הפנים looked like a rocking boat
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about four forked golden supports that held the bread

steps.title: Was the showbread disqualified during the desert journeys?
steps.stepSummary: A new question: when the משכן traveled, did the bread on the שולחן become פסול because it left its holy place?
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: Does the לחם הפנים become disqualified during the journeys, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a brand-new topic. It asks what happened to the לחם הפנים when the משכן was taken apart and carried.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Holy bread normally becomes פסול if it leaves its holy area. This is called יוצא. During the journeys, the bread was carried on the שולחן outside its usual place. The question is whether the normal rule still applies then.

keyTerms.meaning: "It was asked of them". This opens a real open question.
The showbread placed on the שולחן
Becomes disqualified
The journeys of בני ישראל in the desert

phrases.english: A question was asked of them: the showbread,
is it disqualified during the journeys,
or is it not disqualified during the journeys?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the shape topic and starts a new question
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether carrying the משכן during the journeys makes the לחם הפנים פסול

steps.title: רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי disagree
steps.stepSummary: Two אמוראים disagree. One says the bread becomes פסול, and the other says it does not. We are not told who holds which view.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי disagree. One says it is disqualified, and one says it is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports that this question is a real argument between two great אמוראים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase "חד אמר... וחד אמר" means we know both opinions but not which sage said which. This sets up the next step, where the גמרא explains each side's reasoning.

keyTerms.meaning: "One said... and one said". Two opinions, without telling us who said which.
Is not disqualified

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume רבי יוחנן holds the first view just because he is named first. The גמרא does not say who holds which side.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי –
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi:
one said: it is disqualified,
and one said: it is not disqualified.

steps.triggerLanguage: חַד אָמַר: נִפְסָל, וְחַד אָמַר: אֵינוֹ נִפְסָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reports the argument over the question of step 4
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One אמורא says the לחם הפנים becomes פסול during the journeys. The other says it does not.

steps.title: Source for the view that the bread is disqualified
steps.stepSummary: The view that the bread becomes פסול learns it from the פסוק "כאשר יחנו כן יסעו". Traveling is treated just like camping.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says it is disqualified learns it from the פסוק "As they camp, so they travel". Just as when camped, the bread becomes פסול if it goes out, so too when traveling, it becomes פסול if it goes out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source for the opinion that the bread becomes פסול during the journeys.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק puts camping and traveling side by side. This shows they have the same rules. When the משכן is set up, bread taken out of its area becomes פסול. So the same must be true while traveling.

keyTerms.meaning: "As they camp, so they travel" (במדבר ב:יז)
Camping: when the משכן is set up in one place
Traveling: when the משכן is taken apart and carried
Something holy that went out of its permitted area and became פסול

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the holiness rules of the משכן did not simply turn off during travel. The other opinion will need a different reading of this פסוק.

phrases.english: The one who says it is disqualified:
as it is written: "As they camp, so shall they travel."
phrases.notes: במדבר 2:17

phrases.english: Just as when it is camped, it is disqualified by going out,
so too when it travels, it is disqualified by going out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the first opinion in step 5
steps.raayaObject: The view that the לחם הפנים becomes פסול during the journeys
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק "כאשר יחנו כן יסעו" (במדבר ב:יז), which compares traveling to camping

steps.title: The source for the view that the bread is not disqualified
steps.stepSummary: The view that the bread stays kosher learns it from the פסוק "ולחם התמיד עליו יהיה".
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says the bread is not disqualified learns it from the פסוק: "And the constant bread shall be on it."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives the source for the second view, that the bread does not become פסול while traveling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This פסוק is about the משכן being packed up for a journey. It still calls the bread on the שולחן "the constant bread". That means the bread keeps its holy status even while it travels.

keyTerms.meaning: The 'constant bread', meaning the לחם הפנים that is always on the שולחן
It does not become disqualified
Shall be on it, on the שולחן

phrases.english: The one who says it is not disqualified
as it is written: "And the constant bread shall be on it."
phrases.notes: במדבר 4:7. This פסוק talks about covering the שולחן for travel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel to step 6. Step 6 gave the פסוק for one view, and this step gives the פסוק for the other view.
steps.raayaObject: The view that the bread is not פסול during travel

steps.title: What does the lenient view do with 'as they camp so they travel'?
steps.stepSummary: The view that the bread is not פסול is challenged: the פסוק "כאשר יחנו כן יסעו" is also written in the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one too: isn't it written, "As they camp, so shall they travel"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the lenient view. That view must also explain the פסוק the strict view relied on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 6, the strict view used "כאשר יחנו כן יסעו" to compare traveling to camping. The question is how the lenient view deals with that comparison. It seems to point toward the bread becoming פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one, the other side of the argument
Also, too

phrases.english: And the other one too,
phrases.notes: 'The other one' here means the view that says the bread is NOT פסול.

phrases.english: isn't it written: "As they camp, so shall they travel"?
phrases.notes: במדבר 2:17

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the strict view's פסוק from step 6 against the lenient view from step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that the bread is not פסול
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תורה compares traveling to camping. While camping, bread that leaves its place is פסול. So it seems traveling should also make the bread פסול.

steps.title: The lenient view reads the comparison the other way
steps.stepSummary: The lenient view uses the same comparison in the opposite direction. During camping, bread that stays in place is fine, so during travel, bread that stays in place is also fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: He reads it the other way: just as while camping, if the bread did not leave its place, it is not disqualified, so too while traveling, if it did not leave its place, it is not disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: The lenient view answers by agreeing that traveling is like camping. It just uses the comparison to reach the opposite result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The comparison works in both directions. The lenient view focuses on the part that is equal: in both cases the bread never left its place on the שולחן. The whole שולחן moved with the bread on it, so nothing was 'taken out', and the bread stays kosher.

keyTerms.meaning: To the other side, meaning reading it in the opposite direction
Camping, when the משכן is set up in one place
Traveling, when the משכן is on the move
It did not leave its place

phrases.english: The other way around:
just as when it is camped,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי לֹא יָצָא מִמְּקוֹמוֹ – לָא מִיפְּסֵיל,
phrases.english: when it did not leave its place, it is not disqualified,
so too when it travels,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי לֹא יָצָא מִמְּקוֹמוֹ – לָא מִיפְּסֵיל.
phrases.english: when it did not leave its place, it is not disqualified.
phrases.notes: 'Its place' means on the שולחן. The bread rides along on the שולחן, so it never really left.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reverses the direction of the comparison: same פסוק, opposite conclusion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought comparing traveling to camping must mean the bread becomes פסול
steps.terutzMaskana: The comparison can mean that bread which stays in its place is kosher in both cases
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows one comparison in the תורה being used by both sides to reach opposite results.

steps.title: What does the strict view do with 'the constant bread shall be on it'?
steps.stepSummary: The strict view is challenged with the lenient view's פסוק, "ולחם התמיד עליו יהיה". The next step responds by giving a new understanding of the whole argument.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one too: isn't it written, "And the constant bread shall be on it"?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא challenges the strict view with the פסוק from step 7.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה clearly calls the bread 'constant' while it is on the שולחן during travel. That seems to say it stays holy, which goes against the strict view. The גמרא does not answer within the old understanding. Instead, step 11 gives a new explanation of the whole argument.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it written? Used to bring a פסוק as a challenge
Constant, ongoing

steps.confusionAlert: 'וְאִידַּךְ' here points to the opposite person from step 8. In step 8 it meant the lenient view. Here it means the strict view.

phrases.english: And the other one too,
phrases.notes: This time 'the other one' is the view that says the bread IS פסול.

phrases.english: isn't it written: "And the constant bread shall be on it"?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ נָמֵי, הָא כְּתִיב ״וְלֶחֶם הַתָּמִיד עָלָיו יִהְיֶה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors step 8, this time against the other side.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that the bread becomes פסול during travel
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק calls the bread on the traveling שולחן 'constant bread', so it must still be holy and kosher.

steps.title: רב דימי: they only argue when the bread was taken off the table
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי explains the argument in a new way. If the bread is arranged on the שולחן, everyone agrees it is kosher. They only argue when the bread was removed from the שולחן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, when רב דימי came, he said: when the bread is arranged on the table, everyone agrees. They argue only when it is removed.
steps.whatsHappening: The challenge in step 10 had no answer. So the גמרא drops its first understanding of the argument and brings רב דימי's new version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this new version, the פסוק "ולחם התמיד עליו יהיה" fits everyone. When the bread is 'on it' (on the שולחן), no one says it is פסול. The argument now covers only bread that was taken off the שולחן before the journey.

keyTerms.meaning: When he came, usually from ארץ ישראל to בבל, bringing a teaching
Arranged, with the bread still set out on the שולחן
Removed, with the bread taken off the שולחן
Everyone agrees; there is no argument

steps.whatToRemember: In רב דימי's version, bread left on the שולחן while traveling is kosher according to everyone. The argument is only about bread taken off the שולחן. Later, in step 23, רבין gives a different version.
steps.confusionAlert: The word 'אֶלָּא' tells you the גמרא is throwing out its earlier understanding of the argument. It is not adding a small detail to it.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא, כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי אָמַר:
phrases.english: Rather, when רב דימי came, he said:
when it is arranged on the table, everyone agrees it is not disqualified,
rather, where they disagree is when it is removed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the unanswered challenge in step 10 by redefining which case the argument is about.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrows the case of the argument
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The argument seemed to be about bread arranged on the שולחן while traveling
steps.terutzMaskana: The argument is only about bread that was removed from the שולחן. Arranged bread is kosher according to everyone.
steps.whyThisMatters: This new framing lets both פסוקים work for both sides, and it sets up the reasoning given in step 12.

steps.title: Why removed bread becomes disqualified while traveling
steps.stepSummary: The strict view, in רב דימי's version, learns from "כאשר יחנו כן יסעו". Just as bread that goes out while camping is פסול, bread that goes out while traveling is also פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says it is disqualified learns it from "As they camp, so shall they travel": just as while camping it becomes disqualified by going out, so too while traveling it becomes disqualified by going out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains the strict view's reasoning in the new case, where the bread was removed from the שולחן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that holy items become פסול when they go out of their proper area (יוצא) also applies during travel. So bread taken off the שולחן counts as having 'gone out' and becomes פסול. The comparison now works for the strict view, and the פסוק of step 7 no longer contradicts it.

keyTerms.meaning: Something holy that 'went out' of its proper area, which makes it פסול
It becomes disqualified
'Just as ... so too', the formula for comparing two cases

phrases.english: The one who says it is disqualified
learns it from what is written: "As they camp, so shall they travel":
just as when camped it is disqualified by going out,
so too when traveling it is disqualified by going out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the strict view's source within רב דימי's new framing from step 11.
steps.raayaObject: The view that bread removed from the שולחן becomes פסול during travel

steps.title: The lenient view's source: it is still the Tent of Meeting
steps.stepSummary: The view that the bread is not פסול learns from "ונסע אהל מועד". Even when it travels, it is still called אהל מועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who says the bread is not disqualified, the source is the פסוק "Then the Tent of Meeting shall journey." Even though it is traveling, it is still the Tent of Meeting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives the lenient view's source, matching the strict view's source from the previous step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק still calls the traveling משכן an "אהל מועד". So its holiness has not stopped. That means bread removed from the שולחן during travel has not left a holy place, and it stays kosher.

keyTerms.meaning: It does not become disqualified
The Tent of Meeting, meaning the משכן
Even though it traveled

phrases.english: According to the one who says it is not disqualified,
as it is written: "Then the Tent of Meeting shall journey"
phrases.notes: במדבר 2:17

phrases.english: even though it has traveled,
it is still the Tent of Meeting.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the lenient view's source, parallel to the strict view's source in step 12.
steps.raayaObject: Bread removed from the שולחן during travel is not פסול
steps.raayaSupportSource: "ונסע אהל מועד" (במדבר 2:17): it keeps the name אהל מועד while traveling

steps.title: Challenging the lenient view with "As they encamp, so shall they journey"
steps.stepSummary: The lenient view is challenged with the strict view's פסוק, "כאשר יחנו כן יסעו".
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one, too: isn't it written "As they encamp, so shall they journey"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the lenient view: what does it do with the strict view's פסוק?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The strict view used this פסוק to compare traveling to camping: bread that goes out while camping is פסול, so it is also פסול while traveling. The lenient view seems to ignore that comparison.

keyTerms.meaning: Also, too
But isn't it written?
As they camp, so shall they travel

phrases.english: And the other one, too:
phrases.notes: Here "the other one" is the lenient view, the one who says the bread stays kosher.

phrases.english: isn't it written: "As they encamp, so shall they journey"?
phrases.notes: במדבר 2:17

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the lenient view from step 13 using the strict view's פסוק from step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The lenient view in רב דימי's version
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תורה compares traveling to camping. Since removed bread is פסול during camping, it should be פסול during travel too.

steps.title: Reading the comparison the other way
steps.stepSummary: The lenient view reverses the comparison. While camping, bread not taken out is fine, so while traveling, bread not taken out is also fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: It goes the other way: just as while camping, if it is not taken out it is not disqualified, so too while traveling, if it is not taken out it is not disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: The lenient view answers. It accepts the comparison but uses it to support its own position.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both views accept that traveling is like camping. The lenient view holds that bread removed from the שולחן during travel has not really been "taken out", because it is still within the holy משכן. Like bread that stays in place while camping, it stays kosher.

keyTerms.meaning: In the other direction
Camping, the time the משכן stood in place
Traveling, the time the משכן was on the move
Takes out
Becomes disqualified

steps.confusionAlert: Both views use the same פסוק, "כאשר יחנו כן יסעו". They agree that traveling is compared to camping. They only disagree about which side of camping the comparison points to: bread that goes out, or bread that stays in.

phrases.english: It goes in the other direction:
just as while it is camped,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי לָא מַפֵּיק לֵיהּ לָא מִיפְּסֵיל
phrases.english: when one does not take it out, it is not disqualified,
so too while it is traveling,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי לָא מַפֵּיק לֵיהּ לָא מִיפְּסֵיל
phrases.english: when one does not take it out, it is not disqualified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reverses the direction of the comparison in the same פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The comparison to camping makes removed bread פסול during travel.
steps.terutzMaskana: The comparison teaches that bread not taken out stays kosher during travel, just as during camping.

steps.title: Challenging the strict view with "Then the Tent of Meeting shall journey"
steps.stepSummary: The strict view is challenged with the lenient view's פסוק, "ונסע אהל מועד".
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one, too: isn't it written "Then the Tent of Meeting shall journey"?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא turns around and asks the strict view what it does with the lenient view's פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק still calls the traveling משכן "אהל מועד", which suggests it keeps its holiness. If so, why should bread removed from the שולחן during travel be פסול?

keyTerms.meaning: But it is written
And it shall travel

phrases.english: And the other one, too:
phrases.notes: This time "the other one" is the strict view, the one who says the bread becomes פסול.

phrases.english: but it is written: "Then the Tent of Meeting shall journey"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors step 14, now attacking the strict view with the lenient view's פסוק from step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The strict view in רב דימי's version
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק calls it אהל מועד even while traveling, so it is still holy and the bread should not become פסול.

steps.title: That פסוק teaches the order of the banners
steps.stepSummary: The strict view answers that "ונסע אהל מועד" teaches where the משכן traveled among the tribal banners. It does not teach anything about holiness.
steps.simpleTranslation: That פסוק comes to teach about the banners.
steps.whatsHappening: The strict view answers by giving the פסוק a different job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the strict view, the פסוק tells us where the משכן was placed in the marching order of the tribes. Since it is busy teaching that, it says nothing about whether the משכן keeps its holiness while traveling.

keyTerms.meaning: Banners: the tribal groups that camped and marched under their flags
It comes to teach this

phrases.english: That verse comes to teach about the banners.
phrases.notes: He means it teaches where the משכן traveled in relation to the tribes' banners.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the פסוק a different purpose
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "ונסע אהל מועד" teaches that the משכן stays holy while traveling.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק only teaches where the משכן stood among the banners while traveling.

steps.title: Where does the lenient view learn the banners rule?
steps.stepSummary: The lenient view uses "ונסע אהל מועד" for holiness, so the גמרא asks where it learns the position among the banners.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one? Where does he learn the order of the banners from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question to the lenient view. If its פסוק is used for holiness, where does the banners rule come from?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both views must agree that the תורה teaches where the משכן traveled among the banners. The strict view just showed where that comes from, so the lenient view now needs a different source.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one? Here, a short way of asking how the other view learns this

phrases.english: And the other one?
phrases.notes: The lenient view used this פסוק for holiness, so where does he learn about the banners?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on step 17 by asking the lenient view for its source for the banners rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The lenient view's source for the position of the משכן among the banners

steps.title: From "the camp of the Levites in the midst of the camps"
steps.stepSummary: The lenient view learns the banners rule from the next words of the פסוק, "מחנה הלוים בתוך המחנות".
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from "the camp of the Levites in the midst of the camps."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the lenient view gets the banners rule from a different phrase in the same פסוק. That leaves "ונסע אהל מועד" free to teach holiness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase "מחנה הלוים בתוך המחנות" already says the משכן and the Levites traveled in the middle of the tribes. So the lenient view does not need "ונסע אהל מועד" for the banners and can use it to show the traveling משכן stays holy.

keyTerms.meaning: The camp of the Levites
In the middle of the camps
It is learned from, it comes out of

steps.whatToRemember: In רב דימי's version, both views agree that traveling is compared to camping. The strict view learns from "כאשר יחנו כן יסעו" that removed bread is פסול and uses "ונסע אהל מועד" for the banners. The lenient view reverses the comparison and uses "ונסע אהל מועד" to teach that the משכן stays holy while traveling. It learns the banners rule from "מחנה הלוים בתוך המחנות".

phrases.english: From "the camp of the Levites in the midst of the camps"
phrases.notes: במדבר 2:17. It is the same פסוק, just the next words.

phrases.english: he learns it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The lenient view learns the banners rule from "מחנה הלוים בתוך המחנות".

steps.title: A ברייתא says holy foods become disqualified when the משכן is taken apart
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא: when the camp is taken apart for travel, קדשים become פסול as יוצא. Doesn't that include the לחם הפנים too?
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a ברייתא: When the משכן is taken apart for the journeys, holy foods become disqualified because they count as having gone out, and זבים and מצורעים are sent outside their boundaries. Doesn't this include even the לחם הפנים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the lenient view, which says the לחם הפנים is not disqualified during travel, using a ברייתא that says holy foods are disqualified.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the curtains come down, the area no longer counts as a holy courtyard, so קדשים inside it count as having 'gone out' (יוצא). The ברייתא speaks about קדשים in general with no exception. That seems to include the לחם הפנים and to contradict the lenient view.

keyTerms.meaning: Taking the משכן apart to start a journey
Holy food that has left its proper holy area, which makes it פסול
People with certain kinds of impurity who must stay outside certain camps
Their boundaries, meaning the camps they are not allowed into

phrases.english: They raised an objection: At the time of dismantling for the journeys,
sacrificial foods are disqualified as having gone out,
phrases.notes: Once the courtyard curtains come down, the food is treated as if it left the holy area.

phrases.english: and zavim and lepers
are sent outside their boundaries.
Is it not referring even to the showbread?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After both views have explained their פסוקים, the גמרא now tests the lenient view against a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The lenient view in רב דימי's version, that even לחם הפנים removed from the שולחן is not disqualified during travel.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says all קדשים become פסול when the משכן is taken apart, and that should include the לחם הפנים.

steps.title: The ברייתא does not include the showbread
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא means all קדשים except the לחם הפנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it means all holy foods except the לחם הפנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the lenient view by reading the ברייתא as leaving out the לחם הפנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer limits the ברייתא: other קדשים become פסול, but the לחם הפנים is a special exception. The next step will ask whether this exception makes sense.

keyTerms.meaning: Except for
The showbread kept on the שלחן in the משכן

phrases.english: No, except for the showbread.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 20 by narrowing the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא covers all קדשים, including the לחם הפנים.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא covers all קדשים except the לחם הפנים.

steps.title: Either way, the showbread cannot be different
steps.stepSummary: Using a מה נפשך argument, the גמרא shows the exception makes no sense. Either the משכן keeps its holiness on the move or it does not, and that should apply to all קדשים equally.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whichever way you look at it: if 'אהל מועד' is meant exactly, then even other קדשים should not be disqualified. If 'אהל מועד' is not meant exactly, then even the לחם הפנים should be disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 21 and shows that you cannot treat the לחם הפנים differently from other קדשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lenient view learned from 'ונסע אהל מועד' that the משכן keeps its holy status while traveling. If that is true, no קדשים should become פסול as יוצא. If it is not true, the לחם הפנים should become פסול too. Neither option allows splitting the לחם הפנים from other קדשים.

keyTerms.meaning: Whichever way you take it, a two-sided challenge
Meant exactly and literally
Not meant exactly

steps.confusionAlert: This is not an attack on the ברייתא itself. It attacks the answer that the ברייתא leaves out the לחם הפנים.

phrases.english: Whichever way you look at it,
if "Tent of Meeting" is meant exactly,
phrases.notes: This is the פסוק 'ונסע אהל מועד' from the earlier steps (במדבר 2:17).

phrases.english: then even sacrificial foods too should not be disqualified;
if "Tent of Meeting" is not meant exactly,
then even the showbread too should be disqualified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the תירוץ of Step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the ברייתא excludes only the לחם הפנים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The status of the traveling משכן applies equally to all קדשים, so there is no basis to separate the לחם הפנים from the rest.

steps.title: רבין: arranged bread versus removed bread
steps.stepSummary: רבין explains there is no real dispute. The lenient view speaks of bread still arranged on the שלחן, and the strict view speaks of bread already taken off it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, when רבין came he said: One master spoke about bread that is arranged on the שלחן, and the other master spoke about bread that was removed, and they do not disagree.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the first answer fell, the גמרא brings רבין, who resolves things by showing the two views are talking about different cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bread still arranged on the שלחן travels with the שלחן and is not disqualified. Bread already taken off the שלחן is disqualified like other קדשים. This fits the ברייתא, and the מה נפשך problem disappears, because the difference is not the משכן's holiness but whether the bread is still on the שלחן.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, which signals that the earlier answer is dropped
Arranged, still set on the שלחן
Removed, already taken off the שלחן
And they do not argue

steps.whatToRemember: The final picture: לחם הפנים still arranged on the שלחן is not disqualified during travel, but bread already removed is disqualified. Both views agree.

phrases.english: Rather, when Ravin came, he said:
This master spoke about bread that is arranged,
phrases.notes: This is the lenient view, which says the bread is not disqualified.

phrases.english: and that master spoke about bread that was removed,
and they do not disagree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer of Step 21 with a new resolution.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא) so there is no dispute
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two views disagree about the same case.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each view speaks about a different case, arranged bread or removed bread, so they do not argue.

steps.title: אביי: the משכן could be taken apart at night
steps.stepSummary: אביי concludes from the ברייתא that the משכן could be taken apart for travel even at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Learn from this that the משכן can be taken apart for travel at night.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי draws a new lesson from the ברייתא of Step 20. The next step gives his proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This starts a new topic. אביי is not asking about the לחם הפנים anymore; he is asking what the ברייתא shows about when the camp could start packing up.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this, a conclusion drawn from a source
At night

phrases.english: Abaye said: Learn from this
that there can be dismantling for the journeys at night,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the ברייתא of Step 20 and draws a new lesson from it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משכן could be taken apart for travel at night.

steps.title: Otherwise the ברייתא should have said לינה
steps.stepSummary: If packing up happened only in the morning, the meat would already be פסול for being left overnight, and the ברייתא would not need the reason of יוצא.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if you think the משכן cannot be taken apart at night, when would the curtains be removed? In the morning? Then why give the reason of 'going out'? I could say instead that it was already disqualified because it was left overnight!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי proves his point: the ברייתא's reason of יוצא only makes sense if the משכן was sometimes taken apart at night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Many קדשים may be eaten only that day and night, and by morning they are פסול as נותר, left overnight (לינה). If the camp only packed up in the morning, the food would already be פסול for that reason, so יוצא would add nothing. Since the ברייתא uses יוצא, the packing must sometimes have been at night, before לינה set in.

keyTerms.meaning: It would enter your mind, meaning if you were to think
Why specifically this reason?
I could get it from a different, simpler reason
Being left overnight, which makes holy food פסול

steps.whatToRemember: אביי's proof: the ברייתא says יוצא, not לינה, so the משכן must sometimes have been taken apart at night.

phrases.english: For if it should enter your mind
that there is no dismantling for journeys at night,
when would they be lifted? In the morning?
phrases.notes: 'They' means the curtains around the courtyard.

phrases.english: Why say specifically because of going out?
Derive it instead from its being disqualified by being left overnight!

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ אֵין סִילּוּק מַסָּעוֹת בַּלַּיְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the proof for אביי's statement in Step 24.
steps.raayaObject: That the משכן could be taken apart for travel at night.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's choice of the reason יוצא rather than לינה.

steps.title: Isn't night travel already obvious from a verse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges אביי: why did he need to teach this when the תורה already says the Jews traveled by day and by night?
steps.simpleTranslation: This is obvious! It is written: 'that they might go by day and by night.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אביי's statement that the משכן could be taken apart at night. It says this is obvious, because a פסוק already says the Jews traveled at night too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי learned night dismantling from a ברייתא. The גמרא says no proof is needed, since שמות 13:21 openly says they traveled 'יומם ולילה.' If the תורה says it outright, אביי's lesson seems to add nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious, so why say it?
By day and by night
It is written in a פסוק

phrases.english: It is obvious!
It is written: 'to go by day and by night'!
phrases.notes: שמות 13:21

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's conclusion from step 24 as unnecessary.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's statement that the משכן could be taken apart at night
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק already says outright that they traveled at night, so learning it from a ברייתא adds nothing.

steps.title: The verse might cover only a journey that began by day
steps.stepSummary: Without אביי, we might think night travel was allowed only if they had already set out by day. אביי teaches that they could even start out at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: that applies only where they packed up by day. But where they did not pack up by day, they could not pack up at night. So אביי teaches us that they could.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that אביי's point is not obvious. The פסוק might mean only that a journey already started by day could go on into the night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק talks about traveling at night. It does not clearly say they could begin the journey and take apart the camp at night. אביי's proof from the ברייתא shows that even starting out and packing up at night was allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have thought (the mistaken idea the lesson corrects)
Uprooted, meaning packed up the camp and set out
It teaches us (the new point being made)

phrases.english: Lest you say:
This applies only where they set out by day,
but where they did not set out by day,
they could not set out at night;
so he teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 26 by showing that the פסוק leaves room for a mistaken idea.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the lesson is needed to block a mistaken idea
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Night travel was allowed only to continue a journey that began by day.
steps.terutzMaskana: The camp could be packed up and the journey begun even at night.
steps.whatToRemember: The פסוק shows night travel. אביי adds that the journey could even begin at night.

steps.title: A second ברייתא lets זבין and מצורעין in once the curtains are rolled up
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to contradict the earlier one. Once the curtains were rolled up, זבין and מצורעין could enter the place.
steps.simpleTranslation: And contrast it with this: Once the curtains were rolled up, זבין and מצורעין were permitted to enter there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the first ברייתא, which said זבין and מצורעין were still sent out while the משכן was taken apart. Now it quotes a different ברייתא that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא implies that the camps stayed holy even while the משכן was taken apart. The new ברייתא says that once the curtains of the חצר were rolled up, these impure people could come in. That implies the holiness ended as soon as the משכן was taken apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Were rolled up
The curtains around the משכן
People who are טמא from a bodily discharge
People with צרעת

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two ברייתות. The first says these people were still sent out during dismantling, and the second says they were allowed in once the curtains came down.

phrases.english: And contrast it with this:
Once the curtains were rolled up,
זבין and מצורעין were permitted
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording. Either way it means the same people.

phrases.english: to enter there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new contradiction about the earlier ברייתא's ruling on sending out זבין and מצורעין.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier ברייתא, which says זבין and מצורעין were sent out even while the משכן was taken apart
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another ברייתא lets them enter once the curtains were rolled up, so the camps' holiness seems to end with the dismantling.

steps.title: רב אשי says the two ברייתות follow different opinions
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that one ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר and the other follows the רבנן. He starts to quote a ברייתא that shows their dispute.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: This is not difficult. This ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר, and that one follows the רבנן, as it is taught in a ברייתא:
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי settles the contradiction by saying each ברייתא follows a different תנא. He then sets up the next ברייתא, which will show what רבי אליעזר and the רבנן disagree about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי does not try to make the two ברייתות agree. He says they reflect a real dispute between תנאים. The word דתניא tells us that the proof of this dispute comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult, meaning the contradiction can be answered
This one... that one (giving each source its own setting)
The Sages, the majority opinion

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
It is not difficult;
this one follows Rabbi Eliezer,
and that one follows the Rabbis.
As it is taught in a ברייתא:

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא – רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, הָא – רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 28 and sets up the source that proves it.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each source follows a different תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות should agree on whether the camps stay holy during dismantling.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתות reflect a dispute between רבי אליעזר and the רבנן, which the next ברייתא will show.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that whether the camps stayed holy while the משכן traveled is a real dispute between תנאים.
